paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this one. God was working on a plan for the whole world, and He used a paperwork order from an emperor to get a baby to the right town. Caesar Augustus thought he was counting people (Luke 2:1). God was getting Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem, the city of David (Luke 2:4). Nobody on the throne knows they're in the story, but God does, and that's good news for anybody who feels like their life is just one long line at the registration desk.

Now look at who gets the first invitation. Shepherds, out in the fields at night, with the sheep and nobody else (Luke 2:8). The angel says the news is "for all the people" and that "a Savior has been born to you" (Luke 2:10-11). Jesus is Christ the Lord, and He came for ordinary folks on the night shift, which means He came for you, too. You don't have to clean up first, friend. You don't have to have your schedule figured out. The good news shows up where you are.

Then see what the shepherds do with it. They hurry off to see (Luke 2:15-16), they spread the message (Luke 2:17), and they return "glorifying and praising God" because it was "just as the angel had told them" (Luke 2:20). Mary does something different and just as good. She "treasured up all these things and pondered them in her heart" (Luke 2:19). So when God's Word reaches you, you can run and tell somebody, or you can sit quietly and let it sink in deep. Either way, God keeps His word, and He has more to say yet.
